samples.text: We're seeing agendas that, however noble they might appear, have ultimately postponed what this organization committed to do with the with its founding charter that is maintain peace protect right life and defend the freedom of its peoples we believe in the United Nations and believing in the United Nations means ensuring that the organization discharges its mandate I propose three things reducing bureaucracy and focusing resources where there are lives at stake. We must suspend agendas that are not priorities to return the spotlight to those that really are priorities. We must reform the Security Council, not as a symbolic gesture, but as a vital prerequisite to ensure that the Council's decisions are once again respected and upheld. Chile signed the San Francisco Charter and has been present, ready, and willing to defend all its causes. all of its causes rather. We are committed to the high seas agreement known as the BBNJ and we proposed Valparaiso as the headquarters of its executive secretariat. That means that we now have the first UN body to ever have had a headquarters in Latin America and this is an agreement which brings together many different sectors in Chile to play this role. This housing of this headquarters is an expression of the multilateralism that we believe in, a tangible, ambitious, and able to prove to yield results. There needs to be a multilateralism that is effective and efficient. And allow me to say that the reforms I talked about cannot wait. While we discuss how to modernize institutions created in 1945, we're seeing the emergence of the most powerful technology that humankind has ever known, and no one is governing it. Artificial intelligence is not only a technical matter that we can delegate to experts. It is an ethical challenge and a geopolitical issue. We reject the false dilemma between innovation and responsibility. We do not believe that going quicker is always better, and neither are we going to turn our back on opportunities as a result of fear.

our country AI can amount to and mean growth of between 10% and 20%. As such, we are choosing the path that we call responsible, one of responsible pace. That means making progress as quickly as our ability to administer progress allows. We have regulations that make things possible that do not hamper progress. We have investment in talent and in energy, and we have rigorous assessments of everything that is happening. We want to lead from a position of knowledge and not fear. And I say this in this room for one reason. The United Nations must be able to bring humankind together to discuss a technology that will decide the fate of this century. Nothing can simply be resolved by an algorithm. Mr. President, allow me to go back to the beginning. The president that I talked about that spoke here 74 years ago, spoke on behalf of his people and discarded ideological differences. He said that Chile will continue working fervently and with deep belief in the principles of the UN Charter and the fact that they must be tangibly expressed. We believe in human rights. And at that time, in 1945, we had 7 million inhabitants. Today, we have 20 million. The world has changed, and we have too. But what he said remains relevant. And once again, I say before you that Chile has come back to establish order. With order, freedom returns, trust returns, and it has done. We are Investment has returned and investment brings work. Chile is getting back on its feet as quickly as it fell, and it's come to say to the world that a country can recover, and a country recovers with votes, agreements, laws, and results. But I have one more thing to say, that is that a future can be built without being held hostage by others' decisions. Latin America can be the continent of the coming decade, not because someone gives it permission to be just that, but because we have the desire and the ability to be that country and that continent.

Our commitment to peace is summed up in the words of a distinguished Paraguayan, Manuel Gondra. Since we cannot ensure that the just are always strong, we must strive to ensure that the strong are always just. Paraguay wishes to shoulder greater responsibilities within the system, but this system as it stands simply isn't working. That is why we believe that the selection of the next Secretary-General will be a fundamental decision. The time has come for that leadership to come from Latin America and the Caribbean. Our region has a vocation for peace, dialogue and multilateralism, and it has candidates that are capable of taking up that responsibility. We need a Secretary-General who restores the organization's political leadership, one that strengthens preventive diplomacy, acts before crises become irreversible, and one that listens to the states and the peoples whom this organization serves. In short, the Security Council must cease to be a pretty snapshot of the world as it was in 1945. It must listen more closely to this assembly and must not remain paralyzed when peace is threatened. We need a UN for 2026 or for 2050, not one for 1945. Only then will the United Nations be able to truly deliver for all of its members. This Assembly also calls on us to manage transformation. No one here needs me to tell them what the great transformation of our age is. Every great era in human history has had its driving force. Steam powered the industrial revolution. The transistor powered the digital age. No force in our time is as profound as artificial intelligence. We can already see its power in warfare, in the economy, and in our everyday lives. Unlike tools that merely transmitted what we said, these systems are part and parcel of the decisions that we make. The potential is immense. Paraguay today feeds 100 million people, and with this tool, it could feed 1 billion. It could enable us to cover in years distances that once took generations. This transformation cannot be held back and no one should be left out of it.

Do not invent quotes, countries, numbers or mandates. Distinguish prepared text from delivered text, AI from generic digitalization, and uncertainty from No. Return the strict requested JSON. This is an automated review, never a claim of human verification. Read every representative and boundary passage. Propose analytical theme definitions grounded in these statements. Separate technical AI safety from military/security concerns when warranted. Include minority positions; do not force one theme per cluster or a predetermined number. Every theme needs exact source examples, inclusion/exclusion and boundary cases.
